title: Why Fulham were denied comedic goal in FA Cup loss to Southampton
content:
Fulham thought they had taken the lead against Southampton in the first half of Sunday’s FA Cup clash — and in the most unconventional of circumstances.

Southampton left-back Ryan Manning had provided an accidental assist he knew very little about after Daniel Peretz’s goal kick had cannoned off his back and into the path of Fulham striker Rodrigo Muniz.

Muniz found the back of the net, but the goal was disallowed by referee Jarred Gillett, denying Fulham a comedic opener. The decision was greeted by boos from the home crowd at Craven Cottage, and required a discussion between Gillett and Fulham captain Tom Cairney to explain the ruling.

In the 19th minute of Sunday’s FA Cup fifth-round tie, Southampton were awarded a goal kick after a Muniz header from a free-kick sailed harmlessly wide.

Southampton goalkeeper Peretz took the goal kick quickly, and, failing to get enough height on the ball, it struck the back of team-mate Manning. The Southampton defender was jogging back into position for the restart of play and was one of 13 players from the two sides still in the penalty area when the goal kick was taken.

Gillett blew his whistle to signal for play to stop as the ball ricocheted into Muniz’s path. The Fulham striker half-volleyed the ball into the empty net, and the home side celebrated as Peretz raised his hand in apology.

Gillet immediately indicated that he had stopped play and the goal would not stand. He gestured to his whistle during a quick conversation with Peretz, before explaining his decision to Cairney. The game restarted with another goal kick for Peretz.

“I’ve never seen anything like that,” co-commentator Adam Virgo said on TNT Sports.

Technically, the goal was never awarded in the first place as Gillett blew his whistle before Muniz put the ball in the net.

The Australian official did not confirm why he had blown his whistle to halt play, but it appears to be due to one of two procedural elements of the goal kick that he deemed had been breached.

Law 16.1 in the International Football Board (IFAB) laws of the game states that at a goal kick, “the ball must be stationary” and “opponents must be outside the penalty area until the ball is in play”.

Given the speed at which Peretz attempted to take the goal kick, it was not clear whether the ball had entirely stopped rolling before he struck it.

There were also five members of the Fulham team still in the penalty area when he took the goal kick. The law does state, however, that if an opponent is still in the penalty area “because they did not have time to leave”, then “the referee allows play to continue”.

As Gillet had blown his whistle to stop play before Muniz scored, the video assistant referee (VAR) could not intervene and overall the decision.

The IFAB laws state that officials “must always make an initial decision as if there was no VAR” with the caveat that “delaying the flag/whistle for an offence is only permissible in a very clear attacking situation when a player is about to score a goal or has a clear run into/towards the opponents’ penalty area”.

Asked about the decision at full time, Fulham head coach Marco Silva said: “I didn’t get an explanation.” Silva added he was yet to speak to Gillet about it.

Championship side Southampton went on to shock their Premier League counterparts and secure their place in the FA Cup quarter-finals with a 1-0 win on Sunday. Ross Stewart converted a 91st-minute penalty after Joachim Andersen had been penalised for bringing down Finn Azaz.

It sees Southampton book their place in the FA Cup quarter-finals for the first time since 2022.
